title: Same action, why?
hook: Two matching actions can have different explanations.

knows: Animals can act and respond to conditions.
doesNotKnow: Two animals both open the same box. What additional evidence would best help test whether one copied the other?

misconception: One observed behavior always supports a broad or causal conclusion.
objective: Two animals both open the same box. What additional evidence would best help test whether one copied the other?

claims.text: Two animals both open the same box. What additional evidence would best help test whether one copied the other? Both panels show the same final action, but only one includes an observed demonstration. Comparing otherwise similar animals with and without the demonstration can help test whether observing changes later behavior. A matching action by itself does not prove imitation.
claims.source: Stipulated toy observations; not observed animal data. Source lead, not checked: OpenStax Biology 2e, Behavioral Biology, https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/45-7-behavioral-biology

claims.text: The panels show a stipulated illustrative scenario, not observations or measurements of real animals.
Two animals reach the same food. To investigate whether one learned from watching, what comparison is useful? A comparison with and without the demonstration can help isolate its contribution.
